sections.h2: Fast sale options in Mount Pleasant
sections.html:
Two routes move quickly here. One is a listing priced and staged to draw offers within a few weeks. The other is an as-is sale to a cash buyer, which gives up some price but removes repairs, open houses and the financing contingency.

Homes in Mount Pleasant sit at a high price point. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $788,900, and a roof, a service panel or a permit clean-up at that level can cost tens of thousands. Some owners would rather hand that project to a buyer who wants it.

Either way, start the same folder: your deed, a recent Receiver of Taxes bill, the mortgage payoff letter, and permits or occupancy certificates for any work done on the property.

The town is growing and well off. Population is 45,444, up 2.2 percent on the 2020 base, and owners live in 70.5 percent of homes. There are 15,312 households with a middle income of $142,857, and rent runs around $1,941.

Buyers at this price borrow heavily, and their lenders insist on clean paperwork. Open permits and missing certificates are what most often stall a mortgage closing in town.

sections.h2: Villages and hamlets inside the town
sections.html:
Mount Pleasant holds several villages and hamlets, and your address decides which offices you deal with. Sleepy Hollow and Pleasantville are villages, Thornwood lies just south of Pleasantville, and Valhalla, home to Town Hall, is in the southeast. Hawthorne, Pocantico Hills, Scarborough and Archville are hamlets, and part of Briarcliff Manor is inside the town.

Eight school districts reach into the town, so your tax bill is the best proof of which one serves your lot. Tell buyers early.

sections.h2: Tax due dates and late charges
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes collects for the county, the town and every school district. Your bill shows which district covers your lot.

Mount Pleasant tax calendar and late charges
BillDueLate charge
County and townApril 302% in May, climbing to 12% January through April
School, first halfSeptember 302% in October, 5% in November, 7% December to January
School, second halfJanuary 3110% in February and March, 12% in April

The Receiver cannot waive a penalty once a deadline passes, and parcels left unpaid for 21 months go to foreclosure. You can pay at Town Hall in Valhalla on weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, by mail with a U.S. postmark, or online. A card carries a 2.25 percent fee online, and an electronic check carries none.

If your sale closes after the September payment, the January half still comes due. The town tells sellers to alert the buyer, so write who pays it into the contract.

Valuation, transfer records and exemptions all run through the Town Assessor. Grievance Day is the third Tuesday of June, and exemption applications close June 1.

  • Informal review requests go in writing by the last business day of March, ahead of the June 1 tentative roll, and none are handled between April 1 and August 1.
  • Exemptions cover STAR, seniors, military service, people with disabilities, and volunteer firefighters or ambulance workers.
  • Dividing assessed value by the residential assessment ratio gives the office's market value estimate.
  • Send plans, a description of the work and a cost estimate, and the office will say in writing how a renovation might move your assessment.

Buyers should phone the Receiver so bills reach them. Sellers can ask the Assessor which exemptions sit on the parcel before the deed is signed. Forms are posted on the town's Assessor page.

The Building Department issues a certificate of occupancy or compliance once the permit, fees, final inspection and a notarized Affidavit of Final Cost are done. Electrical work also needs its own certificate.

This matters most for an aging deck, a finished basement or a new roof. Permits are needed for additions, boilers, central air, decks, fences, hot tubs, interior alterations, permanent generators, pools, retaining walls, roofs, solar panels, sheds, storage tanks and stair changes. Unpermitted work blocks the certificate and can bring a stop-work order and fines.

Permit review can take four to six weeks. Filings go through the Online Service Center without paper, and plans must cite the 2025 building code. Removing an oil tank takes building and plumbing permits plus inspections, and tanks of 1,100 gallons or more must be registered with the Westchester County Department of Health. Villages sit inside the town, so ask whether your address answers to the town building office or a village office.

A buyer paying cash for the house as-is can accept open items, which may spare you the clean-up.

Owners with an unapproved basement apartment or an addition that breaks a setback may need a variance. Accessory apartments, site plans and variances go through Planning and Zoning, a division of the Building Department.

A variance applicant submits surveys and plans, publishes the public notice in the Journal News, mails notice to neighboring owners and files at least 15 days before a Zoning Board meeting. That is a long road to take just to sell, so weigh it against a buyer who accepts the house unchanged.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and transfer tax
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. Its fee schedule starts with a $45 statutory fee, and because Mount Pleasant spans several municipalities, a $0.50 charge for each extra town named can apply to a parcel on a boundary. The clerk's own example, a three-page residential deed in one municipality, comes to $190 in fees.

State transfer tax is figured on the price rounded up to a multiple of $500 and is due when the deed is presented. Sales at $1 million or more add a buyer-paid one percent, the so-called mansion tax. Your closing attorney will handle the filings, but ask for the totals ahead of time so nothing surprises you at the table.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
A sale here follows a predictable order. First, collect the deed, tax bills and any permit paperwork. Second, ask the Building Department whether any permits for past work are still open, since those are the items that surprise sellers late. Third, get your payoff letter from the lender. Then compare offers on what you actually keep, counting repairs a buyer will ask for against the discount a cash buyer wants.

At the closing you sign the deed, the transfer tax return and the closing statement. Keep your own copies. If the Receiver of Taxes still shows a balance on the parcel, it should be paid from your proceeds at the table, and a call to that office a few days before closing will tell you the exact amount.

faqs.q: What are the property tax due dates in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: April 30 for town and county tax, then September 30 and January 31 for the two school halves. Penalties start the next month and the Receiver cannot forgive them.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: About $788,900 for owner-occupied homes, set against a middle household income of $142,857 and rent near $1,941.

faqs.q: Does the town require a certificate of occupancy before a sale?
faqs.a: The town issues it when permitted work clears final inspection, and unpermitted work stops it. Mortgage lenders may ask to see it, though a cash purchaser can take the house as it is.

faqs.q: How much do recording fees run in Westchester?
faqs.a: The clerk's example of a three-page residential deed is $190, with extra pages billed separately and transfer tax added.

faqs.q: Who owes the mansion tax in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: The buyer, at one percent of a $1 million or higher price on a residence. Sellers are liable only when the buyer fails to pay.
